notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood Hosted API as quick path then Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation. CTO prefers Hosted for quick start; platform team wants route to Dedicated behind VPC once POC proves unit economics.

Key contact map:
- CTO: Javier Moreno (product/infra owner) — cares about latency p95 and predictable cost.
- Head of ML: Lila Thompson — owns model selection, quantization tradeoffs.
- Procurement: Erin Cole — procurement + legal (DPA/SCC).
- AE: Daniel Ruiz; SE: Maya Patel.

Technical reqs / targets (from discovery):
- Primary workload: chat-assistant (customer support) + search embeddings for product docs. Secondary: reranking for search results.
- Latency: interactive chat p95 target <= 250ms for 75% of traffic; tail tolerant on lower-cost traffic.
- Throughput: baseline 40-60 reqs/sec during peak for chat; embeddings pipeline ~25 reqs/sec.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget — target < $0.03/token equivalent blended across workloads; prefer predictable committed pricing if Dedicated reduces unit cost by >25%.
- Model preferences: open Llama-family variants allowed; embargoes on private customer PII — must support KMS and audit logging.

POC plan (agreed):
- 2-week POC on Hosted API initial (week 1): run live chat load with synthetic traffic; collect latency/token metrics and sample outputs.
- 2-week Dedicated trial (week 2-3): mirror workload to Dedicated pool for comparison of p95, throughput, and cost.
- Deliverable: POC perf report + cost-per-inference model + recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated + suggested quantization profile).

Cost-optimization workshop notes (scheduled):
- Agenda items: batching strategy, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles (int8 vs int4 feasibility), routing policies for premium vs low-cost traffic, fallbacks and model variants.
- Preliminary ideas SE suggested: dynamic batching cap at 64 tokens for chat; group embeddings requests to 128 vectors/batch; 24h prefix cache for repeated help-article queries.
- Quantization tradeoffs: Lila wants QoE baseline — run AB tests comparing int8 -> ~15-20% cost drop, int4 experimental for lower-tier traffic if accuracy acceptable. Need eval set and automated quality regression checks.
- Unit economics example (SE back-of-envelope):
  * Hosted baseline (small model) — estimate $0.045/token at current config for chat under naive single-request.
  * With batching (x3 effective) + KV caching (avoid 20% tokens) + int8 quantization => projected blended $0.018-$0.025/token.
  * Dedicated reserved capacity projection reduces infra per-token by ~22% but requires 6-12mo commit; procurement sensitive to min ARR.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If we can get predictable sub-$0.03/token blended and p95 <250ms, we can move to Dedicated commit." — Javier (CTO).
- "We need a strong audit trail and KMS — that's non negotiable for our enterprise customers." — Erin (Procurement).

Open questions / Risks:
- EU data residency for enterprise customers — need clear Dedicated VPC region plan.
- Legal needs DPA + SCCs reviewed before procurement — timeline unknown.
- CFO wants hard ARR vs pay-as-you-go comparison before commit.

Next steps (short):
- 2026-02-20: Run cost optimization workshop with engineering + ML (SE-led).
- Deliver POC perf/cost report by 2026-03-05.
- Pricing proposal for Dedicated + commitment tiers to procurement by 2026-03-15.

Attachments / links: pricing deck, security FAQ, POC plan (drive links in record).

Notes tone: choppy bullets, action-oriented. Put pressure on quick wins (batching + cache) to hit CFO thresholds.
